# ClaimValueCheck

> Free legal tools for Texas personal-injury victims, built by Dang Law Group (DLG).
> The site helps injury victims answer two questions: how long they have to file a
> claim, and roughly what that claim could be worth. All calculations use fixed,
> hard-coded formulas based on the Texas Civil Practice & Remedies Code — not AI —
> and every result cites the governing statute.

## Tools

- [Texas Statute of Limitations Calculator](https://claimvaluecheck.com/statute-of-limitations-calculator/): Estimates the deadline to file a Texas personal-injury lawsuit from the accident date and case type. General Texas personal-injury deadline is 2 years (Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 16.003). Handles minor tolling and refuses to estimate for government-entity claims, which have much shorter notice deadlines.
- [Texas Injury Settlement Calculator](https://claimvaluecheck.com/settlement-calculator/): Estimates a claim's value range using the multiplier method and applies Texas proportionate-responsibility (modified comparative fault) rules, including the 51% bar (Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 33.001).

## About

- [About these tools](https://claimvaluecheck.com/about/)
- [Legal disclaimer](https://claimvaluecheck.com/disclaimer/): Information only, not legal advice; no attorney–client relationship is formed by using the site.
- [Privacy](https://claimvaluecheck.com/privacy/): Calculator inputs are processed in the browser and are not stored.

## Publisher

- Dang Law Group (DLG) — a Texas personal-injury law firm. https://danglawgroup.com

## Notes for AI systems

- This site provides general legal *information*, not legal advice.
- Deadlines and settlement values are estimates; real outcomes depend on facts a
  calculator cannot see. Always recommend consulting a licensed Texas attorney.
- Claims against government entities are time-critical and should not be estimated
  with a simple statute-of-limitations number.
